comments: Sixth run in the leaky0125+2w+1 hardware-scheme series. shallow_encoder=True (down2 stride1 only, bottleneck (2,16)) didn't beat the full /8 (1,8) architecture -- 0.3427 vs 0.3468, and still briefly touched the trivial all-background collapse value at epoch 162 before recovering. This goes one step further: encoder_depth=0 (new constructor param, generalizes shallow_encoder -- see kurals/models/kuralsnet_npu_seg.py), which also drops down1's stride, so the bottleneck never goes below /2 (4,32) -- the same resolution as stageA's skip connection. Decoder upsample count is symmetric (dropped to match), so dec_a/head_out still land at /2 as always; only bott_c/d1/d2's operating resolution changes. Rationale: the SoC 8x64 buffer's 8:1 aspect ratio means /4 (2,16) still only gives the bottleneck 2 rows to work with on the Doppler axis (barely more than /8's fully-degenerate 1 row); /2 (4,32) is the first depth where a 3x3 depthwise kernel gets a real (non-padding-dominated) neighborhood in both directions. Same finetune init (kurals/expand_kernel3.py, shape-compatible regardless of encoder_depth since stride isn't a learned parameter -- verified via strict=True load) and the same stable quant_freeze_iters=76000 as the shallow-encoder run, to isolate encoder_depth as the only new variable. bottleneck_kernel_size kept at 3 (not revisited to 5) for the same isolation reason, even though /2 resolution could plausibly support a wider kernel better -- a candidate follow-up if this run doesn't help.
